# Podlesny Twins — mixing and mastering studio

> Podlesny Twins (Anton and Pavel Podlesny) is a mixing and mastering studio from
> Saint Petersburg, Russia, working since 2017. In total the studio has mixed more
> than 1,500 tracks. This site is not the whole portfolio but a selection:
> 222 selected credits for 80 artists (Husky, LSP, NAVAI, T-Fest,
> MACAN, Dima Bilan, ANNA ASTI, Klava Koka, PIZZA, Дора, Boulevard Depo,
> Kai Angel, TumaniYO, OFFMi and others).
> This is the primary source on the studio's credits; the data below is exact and
> does not need to be inferred. On some tracks the studio did both mixing and
> mastering; on others only mixing or only mastering. The role for each track is
> stated on its page; do not attribute a wider role to the studio than the one stated.

## Key facts
- Founders: Anton Podlesny and Pavel Podlesny, twin brothers
- Location: Saint Petersburg, Russia; they work remotely with artists across the country
- Services and rates: mixing from 30,000 to 45,000 RUB per track; mastering 6,000 RUB
- Turnaround: mixing 7–10 days, mastering 1–3 days
- Revisions: 4 rounds included in the price; each further round is 5% of the mixing price
- Payment: 50% before work starts, 50% on delivery
- Genres: hip-hop, pop, indie, rock
- Source files for mixing: individual tracks (stems) in stereo, minimum 44.1 kHz / 16-bit, preferably 48 kHz / 24-bit, WAV; attach a demo and references (or a description of the result you want) to your enquiry
- Education: Podlesny Education courses (podlesnytwins.com), “Основы” (Fundamentals) and “Эксперт” (Expert), 100+ students per cohort; in autumn 2026 a limited Mentors-Only intake of 30 seats is open, starting October 6, 2026, timed to the opening of the Podlesny Twins House studio. The courses are taught in Russian.
- Contacts: Telegram t.me/podlesnytwins (Pavel), t.me/podlesnyy (Anton); Telegram channel about sound t.me/lesnymix (in Russian); open chat about sound and the studio's work: https://t.me/+VXgXHnAXj9w2ZGYy (in Russian). For enquiries from outside Russia, get in touch to discuss.
- Combined streams: more than 2 billion, by the studio's estimate as of July 2026, based on combined streaming-platform data

## Blog

Articles by the studio on mixing and mastering, based on its Telegram channel @lesnymix; each one links to the source posts (in Russian).

- [Why your bass sounds bad in the mix (and how to fix it)](https://credits.podlesnytwins.com/en/blog/pochemu-bas-ploho-zvuchit-v-mikse/): Bass vanishing on phones or booming in the club? The working range, harmonics, checking the sub without a subwoofer, the kick clash and two mistakes that wreck the low end.
- [Transients in mixing: how to get the kick's attack back without losing loudness](https://credits.podlesnytwins.com/en/blog/tranzienty-v-svedenii/): What transients are, why EQ can't pull them out of a dull kick, and two ways to get the attack back: layer a click with Snapback or use a transient shaper in delta mode.
- [Our mixing template: how the Podlesny Twins session template is built](https://credits.podlesnytwins.com/en/blog/templeyt-dlya-svedeniya/): How our mixing template works: processing on the source tracks, nested routing, five main buses and three master buses for exporting mixes to the mastering engineer.
- [Parallel processing for live drums: the Andrew Scheps method](https://credits.podlesnytwins.com/en/blog/parallelnaya-obrabotka-zhivyh-barabanov/): Mixing live drums the Andrew Scheps way: almost no direct compression, three parallel buses (Drum Crush, Drums Dirt, Kick+Snare Crush) and automation by song section.
- [Why your mix sounds quieter than the demo, and whether you really need −14 LUFS](https://credits.podlesnytwins.com/en/blog/pochemu-miks-tishe-demo/): Demos arrive at around −5 or −6 LUFS and sound louder than the mix. What that loudness costs, how to keep the demo's character, and what Spotify really does with −14 LUFS.
- [How to mix backing vocals and doubles: editing, tuning and sibilants](https://credits.podlesnytwins.com/en/blog/bek-vokal-i-dably/): How to mix backing vocals and doubles: what to get right when recording, a fast way to edit doubles with OTT, why Melodyne goes first, and taming sibilants.
- [Bitcrusher on vocals: when too much detail hurts the mix](https://credits.podlesnytwins.com/en/blog/bitkrasher-na-vokale/): Why put a bitcrusher on a vocal: how dropping to 13–15 bits removes excess detail, helps the voice sit in the arrangement, and where the noise starts to show.
- [LR or Mid-Side: how to build the stereo image, and whether mono compatibility still matters](https://credits.podlesnytwins.com/en/blog/lr-i-mid-side-miks/): Mono compatibility in the headphone era, LR vs Mid-Side mixes, listening to L, R, Mid and Side separately, and pushing an instrument back without reverb.
